head.title: TEST YOUR LUCK — BREAK THE CORE v6.0.1

div.p: TEST YOUR LUCK / V6.0.1
Break the core. Choose your risk level: harder settings hit harder, repair less often, and are more likely to kill you.

div.span: DIFFICULTY

div.p: TEST YOUR LUCK / GUIDE
There is only one thing in this game: the core. Press it until its integrity reaches zero, then find out whether luck is on your side.

div.span: Click the core or press Space to apply pressure.
On Normal, most presses remove 10 integrity and every press has a 10% chance to restore +10 instead. The slider changes both odds.
At zero, Normal gives you a 50% chance to die. Harder levels raise that chance. If you survive, a replacement core appears automatically.

div.p: If you die, reboot the core to start over. If the core replaces itself, keep pressing. There is no score—only the result.

The core glows yellow in the 50–60% danger band, orange in the 30–40% band, and red at 20% or below. Your LUCK counter rises only when a broken core is replaced after you survive, then resets when you die. The Shop converts replacements into THING$ and lets you gamble one replacement for a chance at two.

Very rarely, the core enters a gold REPLACEMENT RUSH. For 20 seconds it cannot break, and every press gives you +1 replacement. If you do not press the core for the first 60 seconds after starting, a rush is guaranteed.
TEST YOUR LUCK / CHANGELOG
Every new feature increments the version. Here is how the one-thing game became what it is now.

div.span: Introduced the single-core game and the fake crash screen.
Breaking the core now gives a 50% chance of crashing.
Survival automatically replaces the core; death requires a reboot.
Added the start screen and a 10% chance to gain +10 integrity.
Renamed the experience while keeping Break the Core as the game name.
Added this How to Play guide and the full version history.
Added five difficulty levels that change damage, repair odds, and the death chance.
Added gameplay cheats and a code-locked Probability Lab for custom chance numbers.
Put the Cheat Menu beside the integrity meter whenever the core is visible.
Added a fullscreen toggle and automatic fullscreen request when the game starts.
Added a patch log for bugs, errors, and visual glitches.
Repairs now remove stale cracks and clear the overheated state when integrity recovers.
Added danger-color glow stages and a luck counter for replacement cores.
Fixed the LUCK counter so +10 repairs do not increase it; only surviving a break counts.
Added THING$ conversion, replacement gambling, and customizable core skins.
Added a visible pending-replacements balance so unconverted cores are not confusing.
Added a capped /give command for money, replacements, integrity, and skins.
Spacing around /give is now accepted, and gambling is locked during core replacement.
Added no-space /give commands and stopped the game keyboard handler from blocking spaces in inputs.
Added a 0.1% gold-core event: every press earns +1 replacement for 20 seconds, with a guaranteed rush after 60 seconds without a press.
Added a protected reset control for starting the shop progression over with no THING$, replacements, or unlocked skins.

div.p: TEST YOUR LUCK / OVERRIDE
Use these controls to bend the rules. The core must be active before gameplay cheats can change it.

div.button: BREAK CORE NOWSkip straight to the break roll.
SURVIVE NEXT BREAKGuarantee survival one time.

div.p: Enter the unlock code to edit the repair and death chances directly.
Give yourself money, replacements, integrity, or skins. Use /givemoney100, /givereplacements5, or /giveskinice—no spaces needed. Money and replacements cap at 9,999; integrity caps at 100.
TEST YOUR LUCK / PATCH LOG
A record of errors, bugs, and visual glitches that were found and patched while the core kept breaking.

div.span: Extra clicks during the break countdown could trigger multiple survival or death rolls.
A lucky repair could leave the warning label stuck on the wrong state.
Pressing Space while reading a guide could accidentally start the game.
Cheat controls needed a separate state so they could not change the core during a crash.
Added a visible toggle for browsers that do not accept the automatic fullscreen request.
Repairing the core back to 100% could leave old cracks visible, especially while holding Space.
A +10 repair incorrectly increased the replacement counter.
Unconverted replacements made the THING$ balance look incorrect.
A gamble during the replacement countdown could be changed by the replacement event finishing afterward.
The global game controls prevented spaces from being typed inside command inputs.
